summary: Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of London and SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He served at the University of Hong Kong and as a visiting professor at the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from around 1986 to 2004 and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.
Guankong (1903–1989) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at the Ministry of the Treasury and Japan Securities Finance.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn, Münster, and the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and Michael Hahn. She held research posts in India and Japan before becoming a professor at UW–Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate and PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Jens-Uwe Hartmann.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, training under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery, attested in 2013.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and others.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at the English and Foreign Languages University and Harvard. He held posts at Columbia University from around 1988 to 1999 and UC Santa Barbara from around 1999 to 2015.

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell. Attested in 2014, he served as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

Gustav Haloun (1898–1951) was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady. He held positions at Charles University (around 1927–1931), directed at the University of Göttingen (around 1931–1938), and served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Cambridge (around 1938–1951).

Gustav Roth (1916–2008) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Munich and Patna University under scholars including Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, the Australian National University, and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Guy Claxton is a scholar in Buddhist studies and education who served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol from around 1996 to 2008 and founded Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry.

Guy G. Stroumsa is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Voltaire, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Harvard, later holding posts at Hebrew University (around 1978–2009) and the University of Oxford (around 2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and others, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University.

Gyatsho Tshering (1936–2009) was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as its director from around 1972 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda (1867–1954) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928) and Toyo University.
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1968 to 1978. He subsequently served there as an assistant professor (~1982–1993) and professor (~1993–2017).
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan University, attested in 1992 and 1996.
